دَوْسَرٌ A bulky camel: fem. with ة: (S, K:) a camel (M) strong and bulky; (M, K;) as also ↓ دَوْسَرِىٌّ (S, * M, K) and ↓ دَوْسَرَانِىٌّ (S, * K) and ↓ دُوَاسِرٌ (M, K) and ↓ دُوَسِرِىٌّ : (L:) fem. دَوْسَرٌ [like the masc.] and دَوْسَرَةٌ: or دَوْسَرٌ, applied to a she-camel, signifies large: (M:) and ↓ دَوْسَرِىٌّ a strong camel: (Fr, TA:) and ↓ دُوَاسِرٌ sharp, spirited, or vigorous, and strong. (TA.) ―
-b2- A tough, or hardy, lion, (K, B,) firm in make. (B, TA.) ―
-b3- A penis bulky (M, K) and strong. (M.) ―
-b4- كَتِيبَةٌ دَوْسَرٌ, and دَوْسَرَةٌ, An army, or a troop of horse, or a portion of an army, collected together. (M.) And دَوْسَرُ An army, or a troop of horse, or a portion of an army, belonging to En-Noamán (S, M, K) Ibn-El-Mundhir. (S, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
